intro: Two distributions can have disjoint support. Jensen–Shannon divergence compares each distribution with their shared mixture and remains finite.
task: Return the equally weighted Jensen–Shannon divergence in nats, not its square-root distance.
requirements: p and q are nonnegative probability vectors with equal length and totals within 1e-8 of one.
Use m=(p+q)/2 and return (KL(p||m)+KL(q||m))/2, skipping zero-weight terms separately.
The output lies between zero and log(2), up to rounding. Disjoint supports are valid; do not add epsilon.

Use real finite numeric inputs with magnitude at most 1e6, excluding booleans. Vectors have length 1..128 and matrix axes have length 1..128 unless a tighter bound is stated. Leave all inputs unchanged; raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Find the structure
hints.body: Introduce a distribution halfway between the inputs so each input has support inside that mixture.

hints.title: Build the calculation
hints.body: For very small probabilities, form the mixture logarithm with logaddexp instead of halving a subnormal value.

explanation: The mixture gives positive mass wherever either input does, so each nonzero term has a valid denominator even when the original supports are disjoint.
This operation is a divergence. Some libraries return the square root as a metric; keeping the output convention explicit prevents a subtle numerical mismatch.
